text: Can you describe the nature of the pain—does it feel like a sharp, shooting sensation or more of a dull ache? I also need to know if you are experiencing any numbness or weakness in your leg or foot.

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of back injuries or do you experience similar pain during your menstrual cycle? I also need to know if you have any difficulty controlling your bladder or bowels, or if you feel numbness in the saddle area.

text: Do you have any specific weakness in your foot, such as difficulty lifting your toes or standing on your tiptoes? I also need to know if you have any numbness or tingling in the sole of your foot or between your big and second toes.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me perform a straight leg raise test to see if it reproduces your radiating pain. I also need to check your reflexes and muscle strength in the affected leg to pinpoint the nerve root involvement.

The absence of red flags like bowel/bladder dysfunction or fever is reassuring, but the sudden onset during exercise and radiating pain suggest a structural issue like a herniated disc that needs imaging to confirm. I will request an MRI to visualize the nerve root compression.
